procedure.step: The Ministry of Economy and Tourism registers the factory (the exporter must apply before requesting a certificate).
procedure.authority: the Ministry of Economy and Tourism

procedure.step: The exporter completes the application with the HS code, description, quantity and value of the exported product.
The exporter uploads proof of factory registration, the commercial invoice, and, if a trading exporter, the factory's purchase invoice.
The exporter pays the certificate fee online (fee range AED 10 to AED 200).
The exporter submits the application through the Ministry of Foreign Trade e-service.
The Ministry of Foreign Trade processes the application (about one working day) and issues the certificate, or returns it for correction.
The certificate must be issued before, at, or within five working days of export, is valid for twelve months from issue, and covers only one import.
The exporter ships the goods directly from the UAE to India; if transit occurs, it must be under customs control with no operations other than unloading, reloading or storage.
The exporter indicates third-party invoicing if applicable.
The Indian importer claims the CEPA rate when filing the bill of entry and holds origin information, including which origin criterion is claimed.
The Indian importer keeps supporting documents for at least five years from filing and answers customs requests within ten working days.
The exporter keeps origin records, including cost breakdown, for at least five years from the end of the calendar year of issue.

caveats.note: The CEPA rate reduces Basic Customs Duty only; IGST, GST compensation cess, Social Welfare Surcharge and any anti-dumping or safeguard duty still apply.
The CEPA rate applies only if the product qualifies under the rules of origin and a valid certificate of origin is presented.
'+' in the rule is read as 'and' (both tests must pass); the agreement does not define '+', so this is Mansha's interpretation.
'Direct labour cost' and 'direct overhead cost' are not defined in the agreement.
The agreement does not say whether the build-down and build-up methods use the same threshold, apart from the 5-point Ex-Works adjustment.
A product that only undergoes the minimal operations listed in Art. 3.5.1 does not originate, even if it meets its product-specific rule.
De minimis helps only the tariff-shift part of a rule, not the value-addition percentage.
Cumulation is bilateral only; the last production process in the UAE must still go beyond minimal operations.
The agreement says box 8 for remarks, but India's origin rules and certificate form say box 9; India's form governs entry into India.
The issuing authority may apply risk management, including asking for detailed cost sheets and visiting the factory.
UAE law sets a shorter 3-year minimum for record keeping; the CEPA's 5 years governs CEPA claims.

No official page read names the Ministry of Foreign Trade as the issuer of the India CEPA certificate specifically: its service page covers preferential certificates in general, and the India-specific page is still on moet.gov.ae.
Fee bands are in AED and apply to the invoice value in AED; no currency conversion is done by Mansha.
A producer in a free zone is likely not eligible for Factory Registration, which is required before applying for the certificate; confirm with the Ministry of Economy and Tourism.
Electronic certificates are reportedly accepted and uploaded to India's e-Sanchit system, but this is seen only in secondary sources, not the official text.
The Social Welfare Surcharge is charged on the reduced BCD (no CEPA-specific text found).
Anti-dumping and safeguard duties still apply (no exemption found).
